policy.note: Who may decide what. Sent once by `continuum decision init` as the first act of the space; after that the record is the policy, and changing it is a govern act. Edit this file BEFORE init.

body.reason: continuum install: the project root decision space

alternatives: Each context writes Proposal.status for its own transitions
Trigger adjudication on ProposalFullyReviewed, as the brief's J7 literally says

binding.note: Stage 1 binds an acceptance to the whole model state; the scope above is recorded so a later binding can be narrower without changing this decision's identity

consequences: Proposal state lags review/adjudication events by one dispatcher hop (milliseconds locally)
body.decision: Only Submission.ProposalService changes a proposal's status, always as a conditional update on the expected prior status; a late event against a terminal status is a recorded no-op. The PanelDecision workflow is triggered by ProposalScored (published by Submission after its guarded under_review -> scored write), not by PeerReview's ProposalFullyReviewed.
body.rationale: An applicant can withdraw while the third review lands. If adjudication started on ProposalFullyReviewed a withdrawn proposal could reach the panel; only the status owner can establish that the proposal is scored. Raised by the Continuum Architect in the initial-modeling critique.
risks: A future service granted writes on ProposalStore silently re-opens multi-writer status
body.title: Submission is the single writer of Proposal.status; adjudication starts on ProposalScored

alternatives: Modules writing each other's tables
One database per context

binding.note: Stage 1 binds an acceptance to the whole model state; the scope above is recorded so a later binding can be narrower without changing this decision's identity

consequences: The implementation enforces ownership by table prefix and module imports, checked by continuum conformance
body.decision: Identity, Calls, Submission, PeerReview, Adjudication, Notification and Oversight each own their data-store resources exclusively; other contexts read through an API operation or an event, never the store. All stores live in one SQLite file (WAL) in one process.
body.rationale: One writer per fact puts every invariant in exactly one place; one file keeps NFR-1 (local, no paid infrastructure) and lets synchronous cross-context checks be strongly consistent.
body.title: Seven bounded contexts, one writer per store, one SQLite file

alternatives: Event replica of call status and reviewer standing

binding.note: Stage 1 binds an acceptance to the whole model state; the scope above is recorded so a later binding can be narrower without changing this decision's identity

body.decision: INV-1 (call open and before deadline) is checked by ProposalService invoking CallApi.GetCallStatus inside the submit transaction; INV-12 (ORCID verified) by AssignmentService invoking IdentityApi.GetReviewerStanding inside the assign transaction. Event-fed replicas are used only where staleness is safe (applicant id, criteria snapshot, budget envelope).
body.rationale: A replica fed by CallClosed lags, so a proposal could be submitted to a call the officer already closed. In one SQLite file a synchronous read inside the writer's transaction is strongly consistent at no cost.
body.title: Consistency-critical cross-context checks are synchronous in-transaction calls

alternatives: Reuse Declined for screening rejections
Keep Screening and add an eligibility flag

binding.note: Stage 1 binds an acceptance to the whole model state; the scope above is recorded so a later binding can be narrower without changing this decision's identity

consequences: Deviation from the brief's lifecycle, recorded in BDL Proposal description
body.decision: Screening -> Eligible (screened in, awaiting reviewers) and Screening -> Ineligible (terminal, screened out by a program officer). Eligible -> UnderReview on the third assignment.
body.rationale: Declined is a panel outcome only a Panel Chair may record (INV-8); an officer writing Declined would read as an INV-8 violation in the audit trail and the portfolio. A flag inside Screening hides the most important queue state.
body.title: Add Eligible and terminal Ineligible to the proposal lifecycle

alternatives: Refuse conflict declarations after review submission
Automatically void decided awards

binding.note: Stage 1 binds an acceptance to the whole model state; the scope above is recorded so a later binding can be narrower without changing this decision's identity

body.decision: ConflictDeclaration is owned by PeerReview. Declaring a conflict revokes any active assignment of that reviewer to that proposal in the same transaction. After the review was submitted but before scoring, the review is voided and the officer reassigns. After scoring, the conflict holds the award (decline still possible). After a decision: unspecified (BDL ConflictAfterDecision, accountable Program Officer).
body.rationale: INV-3 says a conflicted reviewer can never HOLD an assignment, not only never be given one. Refusing a late declaration hides the conflict, which is worse than holding an award.
body.title: Conflicts live with assignments; declaring one revokes atomically

alternatives: Sum awarded amounts from the portfolio read model
Read-then-write check in application code
Loop the workflow back to the chair's decision task (irreducible control flow)

binding.note: Stage 1 binds an acceptance to the whole model state; the scope above is recorded so a later binding can be narrower without changing this decision's identity

body.decision: CommitAward runs UPDATE adj_budget SET committed = committed + amount WHERE call_id = ? AND committed + amount <= envelope, plus a CHECK (committed <= envelope). The envelope is copied from CallPublished and is immutable once a call opens; an award equals the requested amount. A refused award returns the case to the chair through a reconsider task that admits only a decline.
body.rationale: A conditional write is atomic across connections and processes, not just within one Node thread; reading the sum from the portfolio would trust an eventually consistent view. The envelope never grows and awards are final, so a refused award can never later succeed.
risks: A future 'adjust envelope' feature would invalidate the reconsider-only-declines reasoning
body.title: INV-9 enforced by one conditional write on Adjudication's own budget ledger

alternatives: Per-aggregate sequences
One delivered flag per outbox row
In-memory event bus

binding.note: Stage 1 binds an acceptance to the whole model state; the scope above is recorded so a later binding can be narrower without changing this decision's identity

consequences: Delivery guarantees are realized by the sqlite-outbox technology in the binding, which claims ordered, at-least-once and durable
body.decision: Events are appended to one outbox table in the publishing transaction, with a global sequence and a partition key (the proposal, call or account). Delivery progress is tracked per consumer; a consumer's effect and its delivery mark commit in one transaction; a later event is never delivered to a consumer while an earlier one in the same partition is undelivered; failures retry with backoff and park as failed after five attempts, holding the partition until an officer retries. The log is retained and is the audit trail.
body.rationale: NFR-5 orders events per proposal across publishers; fan-out needs per-consumer progress; committing effect and mark together makes an interrupted delivery roll back whole and a replay a no-op.
risks: A parked message stops that proposal's progress for that consumer until an officer acts; surfaced on the operations view
body.title: Transactional outbox, per-proposal ordering, per-consumer progress, park after five attempts

alternatives: Header-only dedupe written after the effect
No dedupe; rely on state guards alone

binding.note: Stage 1 binds an acceptance to the whole model state; the scope above is recorded so a later binding can be narrower without changing this decision's identity

body.decision: Mutating requests require an Idempotency-Key header; the key, a hash of the request and the response are stored in the command's own transaction. A repeat returns the stored response; the same key with a different body is refused (422). Natural occurrence identities (proposalId for submit and decide, assignmentId for assign) make the domain idempotent as well.
body.rationale: Logging after the effect would replay the effect after a crash between the two (NFR-6).
body.title: Every command carries an Idempotency-Key logged in the same transaction as its effect

alternatives: Reject late reviews
Per-call configurable review period

binding.note: Stage 1 binds an acceptance to the whole model state; the scope above is recorded so a later binding can be narrower without changing this decision's identity

body.decision: Each assignment is due P21D after it is made; the stored dueAt is authoritative and a sweeper re-reads it. An overdue assignment still accepts a review (Overdue -> Completed), which carries a no-conflict attestation. The officer may revoke and replace an overdue reviewer. Reviewers accept an assignment before scoring.
body.rationale: Refusing a finished review helps nobody; ADL wait deadlines take a fixed duration; acceptance is where a reviewer attests no conflict.
body.title: Fixed 21-day review period; late reviews accepted; explicit acceptance

alternatives: Expiry that auto-declines

binding.note: Stage 1 binds an acceptance to the whole model state; the scope above is recorded so a later binding can be narrower without changing this decision's identity

body.decision: The PanelDecision human task has a 14-day escalation to the program officer and no expiry; nothing is decided by timeout.
body.rationale: A timeout is not a panel decision (INV-8, HumansDecide).
body.title: The chair's decision deadline escalates and never decides

alternatives: Screening waits for the agent
The agent's verdict auto-applies when confident

binding.note: Stage 1 binds an acceptance to the whole model state; the scope above is recorded so a later binding can be narrower without changing this decision's identity

body.decision: Submission enters Screening by its own reaction to ProposalSubmitted. The Triage workflow runs the EligibilityTriage agent (autonomy score-only, constrained by AgentProposesOnly) and records its verdict as a TriageProposal through an operation; on agent failure the verdict is recorded as absent. Only a program officer's ConfirmEligibility leaves Screening. The agent runs as its own principal with no roles, distinct from the platform.
body.rationale: INV-10. A failed provider must not strand proposals. The first draft copied 'approval: decide-rejection' from an example, which would have described the opposite of INV-10; the architect's review caught it.
risks: INV-10 in ADL rests on the absence of a command-sending tool; a later 'uses' edge would erase it with no diagnostic, so a test verifies the agent itself
body.title: Triage is advisory and non-blocking; the agent holds no command-sending tool and no decision autonomy

alternatives: Role claims in the token

binding.note: Stage 1 binds an acceptance to the whole model state; the scope above is recorded so a later binding can be narrower without changing this decision's identity

body.decision: The JWT carries only the account id; roles are loaded from the account store per request and every API route declares the roles it admits. A route with no declaration fails server startup.
body.rationale: A revoked role in a token claim would persist for up to 8 hours (INV-11, NFR-3). Deny by default is enforced at build time of the server, not by convention.
body.title: Roles are read from the account store on every request

alternatives: A shared audit_log table written by every context

binding.note: Stage 1 binds an acceptance to the whole model state; the scope above is recorded so a later binding can be narrower without changing this decision's identity

body.decision: Every state transition publishes an event carrying actor, timestamp and reason in the same transaction; the Oversight PortfolioProjector projects the AuditTrail read model (per proposal: the timeline) and the Portfolio. Neither reads a write-side store.
body.rationale: A shared audit table would have seven writers (cross-context resource access). J8 requires the portfolio to come from a projection.
body.title: The event log is the audit trail, projected by Oversight

alternatives: Model the event outbox as a domain resource

binding.note: Stage 1 binds an acceptance to the whole model state; the scope above is recorded so a later binding can be narrower without changing this decision's identity

body.decision: The event outbox is technology (binding: sqlite-outbox, claiming ordered/at-least-once/durable), not a model resource. The brief's OutboxMessage (queued -> delivered | failed) is Notification's OutboundMessageStore, unique on (event, recipient), drained to a mail transport that is a stub locally.
body.rationale: Delivery is how, not what; the semantic model stays technology-free and the guarantee is checked as a binding claim.
body.title: Delivery is a binding claim; OutboxMessage is Notification's outbound store

alternatives: Unguarded reconsider -> decline
Loop back to the decide task

binding.note: Stage 1 binds an acceptance to the whole model state; the scope above is recorded so a later binding can be narrower without changing this decision's identity

body.decision: After CommitAward is refused, the workflow enters a 'reconsider' human task assigned to the Panel Chair whose only outcome type is DeclineAcknowledgement (rationale, actor, time). Decision events carry the deciding actor and rationale from the task outcome.
body.rationale: The architect's review found the first shape recorded a decline even if the chair answered 'award' (the workflow deciding, not the chair), and that decision events carried no actor, breaking the audit trail at its most important point.
body.title: The refused-award path admits only the chair's acknowledged decline

body.decision: ReviewDeadline waits for ReviewSubmitted or AssignmentRevoked with a P21D deadline; on the deadline it invokes AssignmentService.ReviewApi.MarkOverdue and then publishes ReviewOverdue. AssignmentService does not itself publish ReviewOverdue.
body.rationale: The review found ReviewOverdue had two publishers and no declared writer of the Overdue status.
body.title: Only AssignmentService writes Overdue; the deadline workflow invokes it

consequences: Awarded and Declined stop being terminal proposal states (BDL ProposalLifecycle); PanelDecision becomes once per review round, deviating from the brief section 4 'recorded once, terminal' wording
rev_completion and adj_case/adj_decision become keyed by (proposal, round); ProposalScored and ProposalFullyReviewed carry the round
BDL r-q013 AwardHeldOnLateConflict is replaced by r-q015 DecisionRestsOnStandingReviews; unspecified ConflictAfterDecision is resolved
body.decision: Resolves ADR-005 vs INV-3 (would supersede ADR-005 if accepted; the supersede act is the owner's). DeclareConflict revokes the reviewer's assignment in every state, including completed, and voids their review in the same transaction. ReviewCompletion keeps one completion row per (proposal, round); a voided counted review supersedes the current round and publishes ProposalReviewReopened. Submission returns a Scored proposal to UnderReview (ProposalReturnedToReview); Adjudication fails closed (no award or decline) from the conflict until the open case is superseded; PanelDecision instances are unique per (proposal, round). After a decision, policy option (c): the decision is suspended (DecisionSuspended), committed budget stays committed, and a Program Officer's IntegrityReview upholds it with a finding or rescinds it; a rescinded award releases its amount only if no funds were disbursed, and the proposal returns to review for a new round and a new decision. Change: continuum/model/changes/adr-017-conflict-void-rereview.adl-change. Record: docs/proposals/adr-017-conflict-resolution.md.

consequences.method: Host model.apply of the option's change to the decision's model

options.name: void-rereview-integrity-review
options.summary: INV-3 holds in every phase: a declared conflict revokes the reviewer's assignment and voids their review; a voided counted review reopens the review round and returns the proposal to review; a decision already taken on that round is suspended for a program officer's integrity review that upholds or rescinds it.

body.rationale: INV-3 says a conflicted reviewer can never hold an assignment and its consequence column says a conflicted review is void and voids the award. ADR-005 keeps the completed assignment and the counted review after scoring and blocks the award, which leaves a conflicted review in the mean, penalises the applicant (decline only) and has no release path. Voiding in every phase keeps INV-3 literal in the one context that owns conflicts; per-round completion and case identity make re-review possible without editing any recorded fact. After a decision, automatic rescission would reverse money with no human (HumansDecide) and could release funds already disbursed; letting the decision stand contradicts the brief section 1. A human integrity review with an explicit outcome honours both.
risks: A budget release on rescission invalidates ADR-006's 'awards are final, the envelope never grows' premise; reconsider stays decline-only, so a proposal refused for budget is not revisited when budget is released
Quorum does not model disbursement; the release rests on the Program Officer's attestation (BDL unspecified FundsDisbursement)
A conflict declared late re-opens a proposal the applicant believed settled; the time window for this is unbounded (owner question)
body.title: A declared conflict voids the review in every phase; a voided counted review reopens the round; a decision on it is suspended for integrity review

body.decision: PanelDecision's escalation publishes DecisionEscalated at most once per case (the escalated_at stamp is written in the same transaction) and NotificationService tells the program officers; a refused award publishes AwardRefused before the reconsider task; placing an integrity hold publishes AwardHeld. All three are projected into the audit trail.
body.rationale: The decide task's escalation clause says the officer is notified, and NFR-8 audits every transition; a stamp the officer only sees when opening the work queue notifies no one, and an unpublished transition cannot appear in the audit trail (review B3, B4).
body.title: Escalation, refused awards and integrity holds are published events

body.decision: Delivery retry and skip, projection rebuild, backup and personal-data erasure require the operator role, which holds no business authority; every operator act is written with actor and reason to an append-only platform log (ops_action). Program officers see delivery health read-only.
body.rationale: Recovery actions change what the system does with business events; giving them to a business role mixes authority (review B5) and leaves platform acts unaudited.
body.title: An Operator role owns operations; officers no longer retry deliveries

alternatives: Automatic skip after N attempts
Allow skipping any consumer
Dead-letter queue with manual replay only

binding.note: Stage 1 binds an acceptance to the whole model state; the scope above is recorded so a later binding can be narrower without changing this decision's identity

body.decision: After five attempts a delivery is parked (its partition held for that consumer only) and an alert is raised (structured log line and optional webhook). An operator retries it after fixing the cause, or skips it with a recorded reason. Skipping is refused for submission.*, peer-review.* and adjudication.* consumers, whose effects guard an invariant.
body.rationale: Ordering over liveness is kept (ADR-007), but a poison message must not hold a proposal forever where its effect is informational or rebuildable (review B6). Skipping an invariant's input (a ConflictDeclared hold, a ledger row, a status transition) would silently break the invariant.
risks: A skip drops the event's whole effect, including state later events rely on (a skipped ProposalSubmitted notification means later applicant emails cannot be addressed)
body.title: Repeatedly failing deliveries: park, alert, then retry or skip with a reason; never skip an invariant's input

Leave the event log untouched

binding.note: Stage 1 binds an acceptance to the whole model state; the scope above is recorded so a later binding can be narrower without changing this decision's identity

body.decision: EraseAccount (operator only) pseudonymises the account, deletes its credentials and roles, and in the same transaction replaces the account's personal values in every retained event payload and the command log with a fixed marker; AccountErased (carrying no personal data) makes Notification and Oversight scrub their copies. Business records are kept and refer to the account by id.
body.rationale: The event log is the audit trail and the replay source, so it must stay replayable; a projection rebuilt from the redacted log equals the live erased projection. Quorum has no key management for per-subject encryption.
risks: Mail already delivered and backups taken before the erasure keep the data until they age out; free text that does not contain the exact values is not found
body.title: Erasure by pseudonymisation and redaction of the retained event log

body.decision: Fixed-window limits held in memory: failed sign-ins per (address, email) and per address, writes and reads per account (per address when anonymous); 429 with Retry-After and nothing applied.
body.rationale: The deployment is exactly one process (ADR on SQLite viability), so in-memory windows are exact; a shared store adds infrastructure NFR-1 avoids.
risks: A second instance would need a shared store; behind a proxy, trustProxy must be configured or every client shares one address
body.title: Rate limiting in process, on failed sign-ins and per-account request rates
